title: Ultrathin alumina coatings on nickel electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction: preparation and electrochemical characterization
content: Alkaline water electrolysis (AWE) offers a route to green hydrogen, but its efficiency is limited by the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Nickel (Ni) electrocatalysts are attractive for the OER owing to their low cost and natural abundance, yet their activity falls short of that of precious-metal catalysts. Here, ultrathin (∼5 nm) alumina (Al2O3) coatings were deposited by atomic layer deposition onto planar Ni electrocatalysts to serve as both a porous overlayer and a source of a predefined amount of Al species. In short-term chronoamperometry, the coated electrocatalysts delivered lower geometric current densities than uncoated Ni, but similar current densities when normalized to the electrochemically active surface area. In cyclic voltammetry, the coated electrocatalysts exhibited a lower overpotential at 10 mA cm−2 (563 vs. 711 mV). The electrochemical responses of both electrocatalysts evolved during prolonged potential cycling, and after 2000 cycles the Al2O3 coated electrocatalysts retained a lower overpotential (653 vs. 735 mV) and Tafel slope than uncoated Ni. Electron microscopy and X-ray based analyses revealed that the coating restructured into a ∼100 nm thick porous oxide layer containing both Ni and Al species. These results demonstrate a simple approach for introducing Al species into Ni electrocatalysts that could be extended to ultrathin coatings of other compositions for a range of electrocatalytic reactions.
